_ssot: Rulings only -- no machine paths and no scan output. Paths live in the gitignored sites.local.json so any clone works in any directory; frozen hashes are never stored because a hash that disagrees with reality is worse than no record at all.
_rule: A skill is either shared infrastructure (exactly one copy, here, reached from every project through the user-level surfaces) or repo-owned (differentiated on purpose, living in that repo's big loop). Nothing is both. A repo holding its own copy of a shared name shadows the shared one silently -- that is what `check` exists to catch.

shared.name: shared-skills-infra
shared.why: The governance tool has to sit under its own rule, or the one skill that can detect shadowing is the one nothing checks.

shared.name: github-delivery-loop
shared.why: Merge authority is host infrastructure, not repo policy: the same four-layer stack and the same two hosts gate every repo. It was already split into a v0.1 and a v1.1, and that split is precisely why the same blockers kept recurring.
